Subject: Splunk forwarder + Redwood private deployment: retention & trace enrichment

Hi Soojin,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. Our security team wants to start a short PoC to validate log/trace export from your private deployment (VPC) into our Splunk estate. A few specific asks to scope the work: 

- Canonical field list we should expect from Redwood events (timestamp, level, component, request_id, redwood_trace_id, user_agent, hostname, message, tokenized_cost_estimate).
- Trace enrichment: is there a standardized header (X-Request-ID / Redwood-Trace-ID) we can use to join traces to our own application logs? Are those present on internal retry/fallback events?
- Retention & PII: recommendation for retention in our Splunk index (we typically hold 90d hot, 365d cold). We need guidance on what to scrub before export versus what you can redact upstream. 
- Transport & auth: do you support mutual TLS to a Splunk HEC endpoint, or will the suggested pattern be a forwarder inside our VPC that pushes to a remote HEC?

We attached a sample syslog schema from our side for mapping. Goal is a 2-week PoC: install forwarder, validate event shapes and a handful of traced requests. Can you confirm next steps and any artifacts you need from us (HEC endpoints, certs, test payloads)?

Regards,
Jordan Patel
Senior Security Engineer, FinVault

From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Splunk forwarder + Redwood private deployment: retention & trace enrichment

Jordan — thanks for the clear scope. We can run the 2-week PoC. High-level plan and notes below; I'll share a short runbook and a mapping doc in a follow-up attachment.

PoC plan (week 1 -> week 2):
1) Prework: swap test HEC endpoint and TLS cert (mutual TLS preferred). FinVault provides HEC URL + cert bundle.
2) Collector: we recommend deploying a lightweight forwarder in your VPC (systemd service) that accepts Redwood syslog/JSON over mTLS and posts to your HEC. This avoids egress to our hosted endpoints.
3) Field mapping: Redwood will emit a JSON envelope with the following recommended fields: timestamp_iso, severity, service, instance_id, request_id, redwood_trace_id, trace_span_id, event_type, user_id_hash (PII hashed at source), message, token_usage_estimate. We'll provide a mapping table for your Splunk props/transforms.
4) Trace join: redwood_trace_id is stable across retries and is included on error/fallback events. We also emit X-Request-ID for immediate request correlation. Recommend joining on redwood_trace_id + request_id.
5) Scrubbing & retention: by default we do NOT export full prompt text. We can export prompt hashes and token counts. If you need full prompts for debugging, we require an elevated data agreement and will sign an MTSA addendum. For your retention plan: 90d hot, 365d cold is fine; we suggest |redaction_level=partial| for tokenized fields unless agreement is in place.
6) Observability hooks: we'll enable trace hooks that inject span and parent ids into the JSON envelope; sample trace spans will be included in the runbook.

Attachments: redwood-splunk-onprem-guide.pdf (contains runbook, sample config, TLS modes).

Next steps for FinVault: send HEC test URL, preferred cert bundle, and a small set of request IDs for test traces. For internal delivery, Kimberly + Marissa — can you confirm we can provide prompt_hash only by default and the wording for the MTSA addendum? Tessa — please note retention guidance for the docs page.

Regards,
Soojin Lee
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: redwood-splunk-onprem-guide.pdf (PDF, 1.1MB)]

Folks — looping you in for the legal/data controls confirmation. Quick internal points I want sanity-checked before I send the mapping doc to FinVault: 

- prompt text: default = hash only. Is that acceptable across enterprise customers as the default export policy? If not, what's the approved escalation path (Procurement + Legal + Security sign-off threshold)?
- redwood_trace_id behavior: it is stable for end-to-end request flows and preserved across model fallbacks. Note: if we enable aggressive KV/prefix caching we may include cached input references in logs unless we explicitly suppress them — we should add a suppression flag in the runbook.
- retention recommendation: 90d hot / 365d cold is fine. If customer requests >365d we should require a data retention assessment and commercial amendment.

Proposed reply to FinVault: confirm mTLS forwarder in their VPC, provide mapping table, and require MTSA addendum if they want full prompt exports. I can send the mapping + runbook after you confirm the prompt hash policy and the escalation wording.

Thanks — Soojin
